In [[commutative algebra]], a '''Zariski ring''' is a commutative [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]] [[topological ring]] ''A'' whose topology is defined by an [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] <math>\mathfrak a</math> contained in the [[Jacobson radical]], the intersection of all maximal ideals. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Oscar|last=Zariski|year=1946|authorlink=Oscar Zariski}} under the name "semi-local ring" which now means [[Semi-local ring|something different]], and named "Zariski rings"  by {{harvs|txt|last=Samuel|first= Pierre|author-link=Pierre Samuel|year=1953}}. Examples of Zariski rings are noetherian local rings with the topology induced by the maximal ideal, and [[completion (ring theory)|<math>\mathfrak a</math>-adic completions]] of Noetherian rings.

Let ''A'' be a Noetherian topological ring with the topology defined by an ideal <math>\mathfrak a</math>. Then the following are equivalent.
* ''A'' is a Zariski ring.
* The completion <math>\widehat{A}</math> is [[faithfully flat module|faithfully flat]] over ''A'' (in general, it is only flat over ''A'').
* Every maximal ideal is closed.
